issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal and concrete animal classes: The problem statement (UML and instructions) and the template's commented Main() usage imply animals are constructed with a single String name (the UML for Animal shows only attribute 'name' and the template Main uses e.g. new Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution repository, however, implements Animal and all concrete animals with a constructor taking (String name, int age). This discrepancy will confuse students about the required constructor signature, and the commented example in the template Main will not compile against the solution constructors.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the constructor expectations consistent across artifacts. Either (A) change the solution constructors to accept only the name (String) to match the UML and the template Main example, removing the additional age parameter (and any age attribute), or (B) update the problem statement, UML, and the template Main example to include an 'age' attribute and show constructors (String name, int age). Ensure all concrete animal classes and the example Main use the same constructor signature.

issues.description: Extra attribute 'age' present in the solution's Animal class but absent from the UML and the problem statement: The UML and textual description specify Animal has a name (String) but do not list an age attribute. The solution adds private int age plus getters/setters for age. This is an unmentioned structural addition that changes the class API and required constructor parameters.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the class attributes with the specification. Either remove the 'age' attribute (and its getters/setters) from the solution so Animal only contains 'name' as per the UML, or update the problem statement and UML to document the 'age' attribute so it is intentionally part of the API. Also ensure example usages (Main) reflect the chosen design.

issues.description: Constructor / attribute mismatch for the Animal concept: the problem statement (UML and explicit instructions) and the template Main expect Animals to be constructed with a single name (Animal has a single attribute 'name' and Main instantiates Seal, Pig, Goat with one String argument). The solution implementation introduces an extra attribute 'age' on Animal and provides constructors requiring (String name, int age) for Animal and all concrete subclasses. This creates an API/name/signature mismatch (different constructor signatures and an extra attribute) that will confuse students: they will implement/expect single-argument constructors per the UML/template, but the solution uses two-argument constructors.
issues.suggested_fix:
Align constructor signatures and attributes across artifacts. Two possible fixes (pick one consistent approach):
1) Make solution match the problem/template: remove the extra 'age' attribute from Animal and change Animal and all subclass constructors to take a single String name (e.g., Goat(String name), Seal(String name), Pig(String name)). This keeps the UML and template Main valid. OR
2) Update problem statement and template Main to include the 'age' attribute in the UML and examples (document Animal(String name, int age) and change the example instantiations in Main to provide an age), so all artifacts consistently use two-argument constructors. Prefer option 1 if the original UML/README intended only a 'name' attribute.
